title: Unique identifier linking in user data store
description: The MongoDB users collection stores parent account data that contains unique identifiers (e.g., user IDs, account IDs) that can link data to specific individuals.

title: Quasi-identifier combination in user data
description: Parent account data may contain quasi-identifiers (e.g., email, username, account attributes) that can be combined to identify individuals.

title: Processing of identified parent account data
description: The system requests and processes identified parent account data for storage in the MongoDB users collection.

title: Unique identifier in user account data
description: The data contains unique references to the identity of the data subject through account identifiers.

title: Quasi-identifier in parent account data
description: The data contains combinations of attributes that are unique to a data subject, enabling identification.

title: Attributable data evidence from stored accounts
description: Stored parent account data can be used to prevent an individual from denying certain claims about their account.

title: Potentially sensitive parent account data types
description: Parent account data may be perceived as highly sensitive and should only be collected when strictly required.

title: Data retention beyond functional need
description: Personal data may be stored longer than functionally needed for the authentication service.

title: Excessive party access to parent account data
description: Personal data may be made accessible to more parties than functionally necessary.

title: Unawareness of parent account data processing
description: Data subjects may not be aware about the collection, storage, or processing of their parent account data.

title: Lack of user control over data processing preferences
description: Users may lack control to set preferences or consent in how their parent account data is processed.

title: Lack of control in data rectification/erasure
description: Users may lack control in removing personal data that is no longer relevant.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal data may be processed than is actually needed for the authentication service functionality.

title: Violation of storage limitation principle
description: Personal data may be stored longer than needed for the authentication service.

title: Insufficient data subject controls
description: Support for different data subject rights (access, rectification, erasure) may be lacking.

title: JWT Token Contains Unique Identifier
description: JWT tokens typically contain unique user identifiers that can be used to link data across systems and sessions, potentially enabling tracking of user activities.
assumptions: JWT tokens are used for authentication and contain user identification information

title: User Data Combined with JWT Creates Quasi-identifiers
description: Combination of user data with JWT token information may create quasi-identifiers that can be used to link data to specific individuals through attribute analysis.
assumptions: User data contains multiple attributes that, when combined with JWT, can uniquely identify individuals

title: Processing of Identified Data in JWT
description: The JWT token contains identified information about the user that is being transmitted to the parent user, which may be processed without additional consent.
assumptions: JWT contains user identity information that is being shared

title: JWT Contains Unique Reference to Identity
description: JWT tokens serve as unique references to the identity of the data subject, enabling identification across systems.
assumptions: JWT tokens are designed to uniquely identify authenticated users

title: Potentially Sensitive User Data Transmitted
description: User data transmitted alongside JWT may include sensitive personal information that exceeds what is functionally required for the authentication service.
assumptions: User data may contain sensitive attributes beyond authentication needs

title: Data Propagated to Parent User Service
description: User data is propagated to the parent user service where it may be accessible by parties beyond the immediate authentication context.
assumptions: Parent user service may have additional access to the transmitted data

title: User Unawareness of Data Transmission
description: Users may not be fully aware that their data is being transmitted to the parent user service as part of the authentication flow.
assumptions: Users may not have clear visibility into all data flows during authentication

title: Lack of User Control Over Data Transmission
description: Users may not have control over which data is transmitted to the parent user service or the ability to customize this transmission.
assumptions: Authentication flow may not provide granular user control over data sharing

title: Potential Violation of Data Minimization Principle
description: Transmission of user data alongside JWT may process more personal data than is actually needed for the authentication functionality.
assumptions: User data may include attributes not required for authentication purposes

title: Linking through parent email identifier
description: Parent email serves as a unique identifier that can link the child's login activity to the parent's identity, potentially exposing the child's usage patterns to the parent or third parties.
assumptions: Email addresses are typically unique identifiers

title: Quasi-identifier combination through email and password
description: The combination of parent email and password can serve as quasi-identifiers that may allow linking of login sessions to specific individuals.
assumptions: Email+password combination may be unique enough for identification

title: Processing of identified data during child login
description: The authentication service processes identified personal data (parent email and password) during the child login process, which directly identifies the data subject.
assumptions: Email and password are clearly identifiable personal data

title: Email as unique identifier for data subject
description: Parent email contains a unique reference to the identity of the data subject (parent), which is processed during child authentication.
assumptions: Email addresses are unique identifiers

title: Collection of highly sensitive password data
description: Password is highly sensitive personal data that should only be collected when strictly required. The system collects and processes password data during authentication.
assumptions: Passwords are among the most sensitive personal data types

title: Unnecessary processing of password data
description: Password data is processed for authentication purposes, but the extent of processing (storage, hashing, etc.) may exceed what is functionally needed for the login functionality.
assumptions: Password processing may include unnecessary transformations

title: Child unawareness of data processing implications
description: The child user may not be fully aware of the implications of using parent credentials for their own login, including data collection and processing.
assumptions: Children may lack understanding of privacy implications

title: Limited control over data processing preferences
description: The child user has limited control over how their parent's data is processed during authentication, with no ability to set preferences or consent.
assumptions: Child users typically lack control mechanisms

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing parent email and password for child login may process more personal data than functionally needed, potentially violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: GDPR data minimization principle may be violated

title: Potential invalid consent for child data processing
description: Child users may not provide valid consent for processing parent's personal data, raising questions about lawfulness of processing.
assumptions: Children's consent may not be legally valid

title: Sensitive child data collected beyond functional necessity
description: Child profiles and user type data are highly sensitive personal data. The authentication service may collect and process more sensitive data than functionally required for authentication purposes.

title: Excessive data granularity in child profiles
description: Child profiles may contain fine-grained personal data (e.g., detailed behavioral patterns, preferences) that exceeds what is needed for basic authentication functionality.

title: Unnecessary data treatment and enrichment
description: Child profile data may be further analyzed, enriched, or transformed beyond what is necessary for the authentication service's functional goals.

title: Excessive data exposure to parties
description: Child data may be made accessible to more parties than functionally necessary, including the authentication service and potentially other downstream systems.

title: Unawareness of child data processing
description: Child users (and their guardians) may not be fully aware of the collection, processing, and storage of their personal data by the authentication service.

title: Lack of data subject control over preferences
description: Child users may lack meaningful control to set preferences or provide consent regarding how their personal data is processed, stored, or disclosed.

title: GDPR violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing child personal data may violate GDPR's data minimization principle if more data is collected than actually needed for authentication purposes.

title: Invalid consent for child data processing
description: Child data collection and processing may not rely on valid consent, as children typically require parental consent under GDPR and other regulations.

title: GDPR violation of storage limitation principle
description: Child personal data may be stored longer than functionally needed, violating GDPR's storage limitation principle.

title: Sensitive video data type collected
description: Video data is highly sensitive personal data that may be collected beyond what is functionally required for streaming approved content to a child user.

title: Excessive video granularity
description: Video streaming may capture more detailed visual information than necessary for the intended purpose of streaming approved content.

title: Unnecessary video processing
description: Video data may be processed, analyzed, or enriched beyond what is needed to achieve the functional goal of streaming approved content to a child.

title: Data shared with predetermined parties
description: Video data is made accessible to a predetermined set of parties (the child user) which may be more than functionally necessary.

title: Processing of identified data
description: The system processes identified data (video content associated with a specific child user) during the streaming process.

title: Revealing attributes in video
description: Video content may contain revealing attributes that support identification of the data subject (child user) or other individuals visible in the video.

title: Quasi-identifier combining in video
description: Video data may contain quasi-identifiers (e.g., location, time, context) that can be combined to link data to specific individuals.

title: Profiling through video analysis
description: Video data can be analyzed for patterns to link data to specific individuals or infer additional personal information.

title: Unawareness of video processing
description: The child user or their guardians may not be fully aware of the collection, processing, or storage of their video data.

title: Lack of control over video preferences
description: The child user may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their video data is processed, collected, or stored.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Video data processing may exceed what is actually needed, violating the data minimization principle under GDPR.

title: Potential invalid consent for video processing
description: Video data collection and processing may not rely on valid consent from the child user or their legal guardians.

title: Linking through unique identifiers in browsing data
description: Browsing data sent to advertisers may contain unique identifiers (e.g., device IDs, cookies, user IDs) that can be used to link data to specific individuals across systems.

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combination
description: Browsing data contains multiple attributes (IP address, browsing history, timestamps, device characteristics) that can be combined to create quasi-identifiers, enabling re-identification of individuals.

title: Profiling an individual through browsing patterns
description: Advertisers can analyze browsing data to create profiles of individuals, inferring preferences, interests, and behaviors that link data to specific users.

title: Processing of identifiable information
description: Browsing data may contain unique references to the identity of data subjects (user IDs, account identifiers) that are processed and shared with third-party advertisers.

title: Revealing attributes in browsing data
description: Browsing data includes revealing attributes such as visited websites, search queries, and interaction patterns that support identification of the data subject's interests and behaviors.

title: Data propagation to third-party advertisers
description: Browsing data is propagated to external third-party advertisers where it may be used beyond the original functional purpose of the AI recommendation engine.

title: Data shared with predetermined set of parties
description: Browsing data is made accessible to a predetermined set of third-party advertisers, which may be more parties than functionally necessary for the AI recommendation functionality.

title: Unawareness of data processing by data subjects
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their browsing data is being collected, processed, and shared with third-party advertisers for advertising purposes.

title: Lack of control over data sharing preferences
description: Data subjects may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their browsing data is processed and shared with third-party advertisers.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More browsing data is processed and shared with advertisers than is actually needed for the functional goals of the AI recommendation engine.

title: Processing of identified data - Government ID images
description: The Authentication Service processes government ID images which are clearly identified personal data that directly identifies individuals.

title: Identifier in government ID images
description: Government ID images contain unique identifiers (government ID numbers, biometric data) that directly reference the identity of the data subject.

title: Revealing attributes in ID images
description: Government ID images reveal multiple identifying attributes including facial features, name, ID number, and other personal information that supports identification of the data subject.

title: Highly sensitive data type stored
description: Government ID images are highly sensitive personal data that should only be collected and processed when strictly required. Storing them in a file system may exceed functional necessity.

title: Data retention duration concerns
description: Unclear how long government ID images are retained in the file system. Storage may exceed functionally needed duration, violating storage limitation principles.

title: Excessive party access to ID images
description: File system storage may grant access to more parties than functionally necessary, including system administrators, backup services, or other internal services that may not need access to government ID images.

title: Unawareness of ID image storage
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their government ID images are being stored in the file system, as this is a backend storage operation not directly visible to users.

title: Lack of user control over ID image processing
description: Data subjects likely have no control over preferences, consent, or customization regarding how their government ID images are processed and stored in the file system.

title: Lack of rectification/erasure control
description: Data subjects may lack control to request rectification of incorrect ID image data or erasure of their government ID images from the file system.

title: GDPR data minimization violation risk
description: Storing government ID images may violate the data minimization principle if the images are more personal data than actually needed for the authentication service functionality.

title: GDPR storage limitation principle risk
description: Unclear retention policies for government ID images may lead to storage beyond what is functionally needed, violating GDPR storage limitation requirements.

title: Invalid consent for ID image processing
description: Government ID images may be processed without valid consent from data subjects, as authentication services typically rely on legal basis other than consent for such processing.

title: Linking through unique identifiers in child history
description: Child history data likely contains unique identifiers (e.g., child ID, birth date, medical record numbers) that can be used to link data across systems or contexts.
assumptions: Child history contains identifiable or quasi-identifiable information

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combination
description: Combination of attributes in child history (e.g., age, location, medical conditions) can serve as quasi-identifiers that may uniquely identify the child when combined.
assumptions: Child history contains multiple attributes that can be combined for identification

title: Processing of identified child data
description: The system processes child history which is identified personal data about the child data subject.
assumptions: Child history contains personal data that identifies the child
